sources.entry: Plonk - Menu bar window manager with snap zones, hotkeys, and saved workspaces that relaunch your apps and put every window back on its monitor; an AI agent can drive it over MCP. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/ostapondo/plonk) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

Plonk - Ten menu bar utilities in one app: a window manager with snap zones you draw yourself, workspaces that reopen your apps on the right monitor, on-device OCR, keep-awake, screenshot annotation, pointer tools and a shortcut guide. An AI agent can drive all of it over MCP.

summary.one_liner: Plonk is a native, local macOS menu bar toolbox (Apple silicon, macOS 13+) bundling window snap zones and saved workspaces with screenshots, on-device OCR, a screen ruler, keep-awake, pointer tools, a shortcut guide, and an MCP server for AI agents.
summary.what_it_does: Plonk is a suite of macOS tools behind one menu bar icon, sharing a settings file, shortcuts, a command palette and a local API. The window module lets you draw snap zones, save workspaces that remember each monitor and relaunch apps on the right displays, and move windows by drag, shortcut or voice. The capture side covers region, window and full-screen screenshots with annotation, pinned live crops, and OCR that copies text from screenshots or paused video without uploading. Other modules include a ruler that measures in points and pixels, keep-awake sessions tied to timers or processes, pointer tools, and a shortcut guide that reads the front app's menu shortcuts. Plonk ships an MCP server and a plonk CLI so agents can drive layouts, workspaces, screenshots, OCR and keep-awake, and each module can be switched off. The README says the project is early (version 0.4.x, one author), and the MCP tool names and HTTP API may change between minor versions.
use_cases: arrange windows into custom snap zones on multiple monitors
save and relaunch a set of apps and documents as a workspace
copy text from screenshots or videos with on-device OCR
keep a Mac awake until a build or process finishes
let an AI agent control window layouts and take screenshots via MCP
measure interface sizes in points and pixels
how_to_run: claude mcp add plonk -- npx -y plonk-mcp
codex mcp add plonk -- npx -y plonk-mcp
notable: Snap zones are drawn by the user, and workspaces restore each app to the correct monitor
On-device OCR and voice command recognition, with no cloud upload
Ships an MCP server, a plonk CLI, and a Claude Code plugin and Claude Desktop bundle
Each module can be turned off, which removes its shortcuts, menu items and agent tools
Release binaries come with GitHub build attestations and a SHA-256 file for verification
caveats: Apple silicon only; the README says Intel builds are untested
Releases are signed with a self-made certificate and not notarized, so macOS Gatekeeper needs a manual step or the quarantine flag cleared
Conflicts with tiling managers such as yabai and Amethyst, which should not run alongside it
